summary: A cast-iron tower on a caisson at the Connecticut River mouth, lit in 1886: its keepers, the 1938 hurricane as its keeper recorded it, and a private owner since 2015.

access.note: Privately owned since the 2015 auction. Reachable only by boat; the tower is closed (LighthouseFriends, quoting the 2008 notice).

facts.agency: Private owner since the 2015 auction (formerly U.S. Coast Guard; GSA auctions in 2013 and 2015)

17-wick oil lamp converted to incandescent oil vapor (NRHP)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends: Congress appropriated $20,000 on 7 August 1882. NRHP: an inadequate appropriation was made in 1883, with more approved later. Both are given in the story.
NRHP: 48 feet. LighthouseFriends: 49 feet. Record: 14.9 m (48.9 ft). Both written sources are close to the record.
LighthouseFriends: automated 1959. NRHP: fog signal remote-controlled from 1958; interior description refers to automation in 1968. Record: 1959. Story gives 1959 and notes the NRHP's 1968.
NRHP: Lynde Point established 1802. LighthouseFriends: first light at Lynde Point 1803. Not used in the story's text beyond the NRHP date.
The NRHP text describes the lantern both as decagonal in plan and as a 12-sided cast-iron lantern; LighthouseFriends says 12-sided. Story does not state the number of sides.

The USLHS archive's person record for Joseph F. Woods lists New London Harbor (first assistant 1911, head keeper 1911-1912), Cold Spring Harbor (head keeper 1912) and Saybrook Breakwater (principal keeper 1912-1918). LighthouseFriends's New London page says he left New London in July 1912. The story cites the person record for the link.
NRHP: Lynde Point established 1802. LighthouseFriends: first light at Lynde Point 1803. The story gives the NRHP date and names LighthouseFriends's date.
NRHP: 48 feet; LighthouseFriends: 49 feet. The story gives both with metres.
LighthouseFriends: automated 1959 (story uses it). NRHP interior description: automation in 1968 (story gives it as the form's date).
LighthouseFriends: $20,000 appropriated 7 August 1882. NRHP: inadequate appropriation 1883, with more later. The story gives both, marked by source.

notes_for_editor: Roster: all 34 USLHS lines entered as printed. Two keepers' wives are recorded as family members with no first names in the sources (Mrs. Dahlman, 1905; Mrs. Woods, 1917). The 2013 and 2015 owners are named in LighthouseFriends (citing press reports) and are not named in the story or here: they are private buyers. The 1938 hurricane narrative is quoted from LighthouseFriends' cleaner text of Keeper Gross's account; the Lighthouse Service Bulletin (PDF pp. 48-49) prints the same account with interleaved OCR. The Bulletin's editors' sentence on the typicality of Saybrook's experience is paraphrased; the OCR is interleaved there, so only the fragment 'undergone by other keepers of exposed' is quoted. Check the page image before publication. The 1939 rescue letter and Woods's 1917 letter are quoted through LighthouseFriends only; no primary copy was found. Dahlman's 1905 accident: LighthouseFriends only. The Woods link to New London Harbor and Cold Spring Harbor rests on the USLHS archive's person record (source 10), which the roster tool joins by person slug; LighthouseFriends does not connect the stations in its text. One Chronicling America search for Saybrook Breakwater (1886-1960, Connecticut) returned four hits, none about the light. Not pursued further. Record claims not checked here: focal height 17.7 m, range 11 nm, and the 'Fl G 6s' characteristic. Not repeated in the story. The 2016 listing and 2017 clubhouse plan are reported in LighthouseFriends from a New York Post article and Hepburn-estate news; kept general; the story does not name the owners. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the 1917 Woods and 1939 Authier passages are quoted from LighthouseFriends; the storm and Gross passages are cited to the Bulletin pages and LighthouseFriends; Dahlman's name is kept from the roster (1899-1907).
